headline: Agentic boom lifts output, hollows offices; compute levies fund patchy new safety nets

events: Spring capability jump: agent systems reliably complete multi-day software, legal and accounting workflows; enterprise seat licences shift to per-task agent pricing
Hyperscaler capex passes $900bn annualised; US and Irish grid interconnection queues explode and wholesale power prices in PJM/ERCOT rise 30%+
G20 inflation re-accelerates to ~4% on electricity, transformer and memory-chip bottlenecks; Fed pauses cuts at 3.75%, ECB holds
Big-4, BPO and insurance back offices announce 15-25% headcount cuts; India and Philippines outsourcing hiring freezes
Ukraine ceasefire line frozen under a fragile armistice; Middle East conflict continues at lower intensity
Second jump: robotic foundation models move into warehouses and light assembly; logistics hiring collapses
AI-equity correction of ~30% in Q2 as agent pricing deflates software margins; capex barely slows because of sovereign and energy-backed demand
US unemployment hits 6.8% with white-collar graduates overrepresented; election dominated by 'jobs vs. machines' and a populist anti-AI-layoff platform wins key Senate races
Central banks cut to ~2.5% as goods and services disinflation from automation overwhelms energy costs
Philippines and Kenya hit balance-of-payments stress as BPO export revenue falls; IMF programmes follow
Wildcard: interacting autonomous trading agents trigger a 40-minute US Treasury market flash crash; markets halted for two days and SEC/CFTC impose agent-registration rules
US enacts a 'compute and automation levy' on large-model inference revenue to fund extended unemployment insurance and wage insurance; EU follows with a harmonised digital-labour contribution
Global unemployment peaks near 7.4%; youth unemployment above 25% across South Asia and North Africa
Gas-turbine and nuclear-uprate orders for data centres lock in fossil generation but utility-scale solar-plus-storage records also broken
Egypt and Pakistan restructure external debt; Sri Lanka-style protests spread in several import-dependent states
Productivity growth in US runs ~3.5%/yr; corporate profit share at record highs while median real wages are flat
Drug-discovery and materials-science AI produce first approved AI-designed antibiotics class and a cheaper sodium battery chemistry
Mass protests in France, Brazil and South Korea over pension and job-guarantee reforms; one Western government falls
Border clashes between Ethiopia and Eritrea escalate into a regional war drawing in Gulf backers
US-China tariffs stay high but stable; a narrow bilateral accord on AI-enabled bio and cyber risks is signed
Re-employment slowly picks up in care, construction, energy build-out and 'human-verified' services; global unemployment eases to 6.3%
Over 60% of firms use AI in production; agent-run SMEs and one-person companies proliferate
Public debt keeps rising despite growth as transfers, levy carve-outs and higher defence spend outrun revenue; US at 134% of GDP
Data centres reach ~6% of global electricity; renewables 43% of generation but absolute emissions only edge down
Debate shifts from 'whether' to 'how much' universal basic dividend; pilot schemes run in Alaska-style funds in three US states and Spain

winners: Hyperscalers, chip and power-equipment makers and their shareholders
Owners of grid-connected land, utilities and nuclear/gas generators
Skilled trades, nurses and care workers, plus consumers of cheaper services, healthcare and software
losers: Mid-career white-collar workers in finance, law, admin and customer service
Outsourcing-dependent economies such as the Philippines, parts of India, Kenya
Fiscally stretched, import-dependent frontier states and young graduates entering the labour market
bullets: World output grew ~3.6% a year, the fastest half-decade since the 2000s, but gains were heavily skewed to capital owners.
Routine cognitive work was gutted first; roughly 210 million jobs were displaced, with re-absorption lagging by two to three years.
Central banks faced an odd mix: energy-led inflation in 2027 then automation-driven disinflation, ending with policy rates near 2.5%.
Governments responded with compute/automation levies and wage insurance, yet public debt still climbed to ~104% of world GDP.
Electricity became the binding constraint on AI: power prices, grid politics and gas/nuclear deals dominate industrial policy.
Social unrest is markedly higher and trust lower, with anti-AI populism a mainstream political force in democracies.
Trade blocs held steady rather than fractured further; compute, chips and models are the new strategic chokepoints.
Climate progress is mixed: record renewables build-out, but data-centre demand kept fossil plants running and warming reached ~1.57C.
wildcard: In 2029 a cascade of interacting autonomous trading agents caused a flash crash in the US Treasury market, forcing a two-day halt and global rules requiring registration of financial AI agents.
image_description: On a grey morning in a half-empty glass office tower, a former claims adjuster in a hi-vis vest trains as a heat-pump installer in the old lobby while delivery robots glide past and a rooftop wall of humming cooling fans steams beside the solar panels.
